question: why the key-event timing gate reports no paired event while the gripper error is a third of a percentage point
method: scripts/so101/e4t_event_smearing.py reads the per-noise-copy predictions the evaluator stores in arrays.npz and counts threshold crossings on the mean prediction and on each individual copy, inside the event-anchored windows
finding: the gate is defined on the mean over the paired noise copies; a discrete close sampled on different frames by different copies averages into a ramp that need not cross both thresholds, so the mean shows 0 of 82 windows with a crossing at 10,001 updates while 52 of 82 windows contain a per-copy crossing, 73 of 79 of them within the 3-frame tolerance. At initialisation no copy crosses at all, so that failure is a real absence of gripper behaviour rather than an averaging artefact
claim: offline diagnosis of recorded predictions; no learned action was executed in simulation
